examples.en: Oil-producing countries agreed to cut oil production.
The factory decided to cut production when demand fell.
Prices rose on news of reduced crop production.

examples.ko: 감산이 길어지면 일자리가 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If production cuts last long, jobs could be lost.

examples.ko: 반도체 업체들이 감산으로 가격 하락을 막으려 해요.
examples.en: Semiconductor makers are trying to stop price drops by cutting production.

examples.ko: 이번 감산은 수요가 줄어서 어쩔 수 없었대요.
examples.en: I heard this production cut was unavoidable because demand dropped.

explain: 생산량을 줄이는 일을 가리키는 경제 뉴스 단어고, 반대말은 '증산'이에요. 보통 '감산에 들어가다', '감산을 결정하다'처럼 쓰고 일상 대화에서는 '생산을 줄이다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The car company has started cutting production.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생산량 줄이기를 시작할 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news when production cuts begin.

phrases.en: The factory will cut production from next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '감산'에 '하다'를 붙여 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 감산 plus '하다' as a verb.

phrases.en: Demand dropped, so we reduce production.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '감산' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday phrase used instead of 감산.

explain_en: It is an economic news word for reducing output, and its opposite is '증산'. It is used in phrases like '감산에 들어가다' and '감산을 결정하다', while in daily talk people say '생산을 줄이다'.

en: to decrease; to be reduced in amount or number

examples.en: Customers decrease in winter.
Accidents decreased a lot compared to last year.
If trash decreases, it is good for the environment.
The rate of decrease is fast.
The cost that doesn't go down is the problem.
The population will keep decreasing.

explain: '감소하다'와 뜻이 같고, 보통은 '감소하다'를 더 많이 써요. 반대말은 '증가'예요. 사람 수, 비용, 사고처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것이 줄 때 써요.

phrases.en: Customers decrease in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감소되다'보다 더 많이 쓰는 기본형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more commonly used form compared with 감소되다.

phrases.en: The number of customers has dropped a lot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 쉽고 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler and more natural word for everyday conversation.

phrases.en: The number of children keeps decreasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 줄고 있는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a change that is still going on.

explain_en: It means the same as '감소하다', and '감소하다' is the more common form. The opposite is '증가'. Use it when things you can measure in numbers, like people, costs, or accidents, go down.

dis.h: numbers or amounts simply go down

p.n: 축소되다 is for scale or size, not a count of guests.

examples.en: The company decided to reduce this year's bonus.
When I explained my situation, they reduced my fine.
I checked whether there is a system that reduces hospital bills.

examples.ko: 소득이 줄어서 보험료를 감액할 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard you can get your premium reduced because your income dropped.
If the subsidy is reduced, household budgets get tight.
The deal was canceled even though the deposit was reduced.

explain: '줄이다'나 구어체 '깎다'보다 딱딱한 말이라서 서류, 계약, 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 반대말은 '증액하다'예요.

phrases.en: Because things were hard for me, they reduced my rent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 사정을 봐서 돈을 줄여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reducing an amount out of consideration for someone.

phrases.en: My allowance was reduced because of lateness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 줄어든 쪽에서 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form from the side whose money was reduced.

phrases.en: Please take a bit off the price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 쓰는 쉬운 표현이고 '감액하다'보다 가벼워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple spoken word, lighter than 감액하다.

explain_en: It is more formal than '줄이다' or the casual '깎다', so you see it in paperwork, contracts and the news. Its opposite is '증액하다'.

examples.ko: 새 앱의 개발비가 생각보다 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: The new app's development cost was more than I expected.
To cut development costs, we didn't hire more staff.
I heard new drug development costs hundreds of billions of won.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 개발비만 오십억 원이 넘었어요.
examples.en: The development cost of this game alone exceeded five billion won.
The government supports technology development costs.

examples.ko: 개발비 때문에 가격을 올릴 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Because of the development cost, we have no choice but to raise the price.

explain: 제품이나 기술을 새로 만드는 데 드는 돈이에요. '생활비', '교육비'처럼 '~비'가 붙은 말이에요. 'N 개발비'처럼 앞에 개발 대상을 붙여요.

phrases.example: 게임을 만드는 데 개발비가 많이 들었어요.
phrases.en: Making the game cost a lot in development expenses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 드는 것은 '들다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Costs are expressed with 들다.

phrases.en: I made it myself to save on development costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 덜 쓰려고 할 때 '아끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 아끼다 is used when trying to spend less money.

phrases.en: How much does app development cost?
phrases.nuance_ko: 개발 대상을 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the thing being developed before the word.

explain_en: It is the money spent on creating a new product or technology. It is built like '생활비' and '교육비', with '비' attached. You put the thing developed in front, like 'N 개발비'.

en: to be traded; to be dealt

examples.ko: 이 책은 중고 시장에서 비싸게 거래돼요.
examples.en: This book sells for a high price on the used market.
That painting sold for 100 million won.
The stock is being actively traded.
Don't buy items that are traded illegally.
I wonder how much the house will go for.

examples.ko: 거래된 내역은 앱에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the transaction history in the app.

explain: 물건이나 주식이 사고팔리는 상태를 말해요. 사람이 주어이면 '거래하다'를 써요. '중고 거래', '직거래'처럼 명사 '거래'로 훨씬 자주 쓰고, '억 원에 거래되다'처럼 '에'로 가격을 붙여요.

phrases.example: 이 물건은 인터넷에서 많이 거래되고 있어요.
phrases.en: This item is traded a lot online.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 사고팔리는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something that is currently and continually being bought and sold.

phrases.example: 이 가방은 중고로 거래돼도 값이 높아요.
phrases.en: This bag is still pricey even when traded secondhand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 물건이 아니라 쓰던 물건이 팔릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a used item, not a new one, is being sold.

phrases.example: 그 물건은 시장에서 거의 거래되지 않아요.
phrases.en: That item is hardly traded in the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고파는 일이 거의 없을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when there is almost no buying or selling.

explain_en: It describes goods or stocks being bought and sold. If a person is the subject, use 거래하다 instead. The noun 거래 is much more common, as in 중고 거래 and 직거래, and you add the price with 에, like 억 원에 거래되다.

examples.en: Today's stock trading volume was higher than usual.
Stocks with low trading volume are hard to buy and sell.

examples.ko: 연휴 때문에 중고 시장의 거래량이 크게 줄었어요.
examples.en: The holiday sharply cut the volume of trades in the secondhand market.

examples.ko: 이 앱의 하루 거래량은 수만 건이에요.
examples.en: This app handles tens of thousands of transactions a day.
As home prices rose, the volume of apartment sales changed too.

examples.ko: 거래량을 보면 요즘 인기 있는 상품을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: Looking at the trading volume, you can tell which products are popular lately.

explain: 주식, 부동산, 상품을 사고판 양이나 횟수를 말해요. 오고 간 돈의 크기를 말할 때는 '거래액'을 써서 구별해요. '거래량이 늘다', '거래량이 급증하다'처럼 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Trading volume rose before the holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고판 양이 많아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the amount traded has increased.

phrases.en: Trading volume surged after the new product came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 늘었을 때 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news for a sudden sharp rise.

phrases.en: Trading volume dropped, so prices fell too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고파는 사람이 적어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fewer people are buying and selling.

explain_en: It means the amount or number of trades in stocks, real estate or goods. For the size of the money that changed hands, '거래액' is used instead. It is common in news as '거래량이 늘다' or '거래량이 급증하다'.

en: to plunge; to plummet; to decrease sharply

examples.ko: 비가 계속 오면 가게 손님이 격감해요.
examples.en: If it keeps raining, customers at the shop drop sharply.
This year's sales plunged compared with last year.

examples.ko: 인구가 격감하면 학교도 문을 닫아야 해요.
examples.en: If the population plummets, schools also have to close.
My income dropped sharply, so I'm worried about living costs.
The number of visitors is expected to fall sharply.
Let's find out why the number of tourists suddenly plummeted.

explain: '수가 격감하다'처럼 줄어드는 것을 주어로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 줄다', '많이 줄다'라고 하고, '격감하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 많이 나와요. 반대말은 '급증하다'예요.

phrases.en: In winter the number of customers drops sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: '격감하다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 글 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 격감하다, in written style.

phrases.en: The number of customers has dropped a lot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in casual conversation.

phrases.en: The number of births is plunging.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 줄어드는 중일 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고 있다' to say the drop is happening now.

explain_en: The thing that decreases is the subject, as in '수가 격감하다'. In daily talk people say '확 줄다' or '많이 줄다', while '격감하다' appears more in news and writing. The opposite is '급증하다'.

en: to settle accounts; to close the books

examples.ko: 연말에는 가계부를 보면서 한 해를 결산해요.
examples.en: At the end of the year, I look over my budget book and sum up the year.

examples.ko: 경리 직원이 월말에 장부를 결산하는 중이에요.
examples.en: The accountant is closing the books for the month.

examples.ko: 올해 활동을 결산해 보니 아쉬운 점이 많아요.
examples.en: Looking back at this year's activities, there's a lot I regret.
The broadcaster wrapped up the year's best songs.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나면 한 학기를 결산하고 싶어요.
examples.en: After exams, I want to look back on the semester.

examples.ko: 내년에 결산할 때 웃을 수 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope I can smile when I look back next year.

explain: 회사나 가게가 돈 계산을 마무리할 때 써요. 연말에 '한 해를 결산하다'처럼 한 해 일을 돌아볼 때도 많이 써요. '정산하다'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 정산은 받을 돈과 줄 돈을 맞추는 일에 더 가까워요.

phrases.example: 연말 결산 방송에서 올해 인기 노래를 소개했어요.
phrases.en: The year-end review show introduced this year's popular songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해의 일을 돌아보며 정리하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for looking back over and summing up the year.

phrases.en: The accounting team is preparing the financial report.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 돈 계산이 끝난 뒤 내놓는 보고를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the report given at work once the accounts are closed.

phrases.en: After the trip, my friends and I settled up the costs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받을 돈과 줄 돈을 맞출 때는 '결산하다' 대신 '정산하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For matching what is owed and what is due, use 정산하다 instead of 결산하다.

explain_en: It is used when a company or shop wraps up its accounts. It is also very common at year-end, as in '한 해를 결산하다', to look back on the year. It is easy to mix up with 정산하다, which is closer to settling who owes what.

examples.en: A big donor gave a scholarship fund to the school.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 고액 연봉으로 사람을 뽑아요.
examples.en: That company hires people with a very high salary.

examples.ko: 현금으로 고액을 내는 사람은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many people pay a large sum in cash.
More students are getting expensive private tutoring.
The hospital bill is a large sum, so I am worried.
It is a contest with a big prize.

explain: 고액은 '고액 연봉', '고액 기부'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 쓸 때가 많아요. 반대말은 '소액'이고, 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '큰돈'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Expensive private tutoring is a burden for parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 많이 드는 서비스 앞에 '고액'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '고액' before a service that costs a lot of money.

phrases.en: It is dangerous to carry a large amount of cash.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고액의'를 쓰면 돈의 양이 큰 것을 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '고액의' clearly says the amount of money is large.

phrases.example: 그 일은 고액 연봉을 받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can get a high salary in that job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 월급이 아주 많은 일자리를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for jobs with a very high salary.

explain_en: 고액 is often placed before another noun, as in 고액 연봉 or 고액 기부. Its opposite is 소액, and in everyday talk people also just say 큰돈.

en: to fall headlong; to fall head-first

examples.en: I slipped on the stairs and almost tumbled headlong down.
Right after the announcement, the company's stock price plunged.
Watching the stock price plummet makes me anxious.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀 성적이 곤두박질하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team's results have been going downhill fast lately.
The bird sees its food and dives headfirst into the water.

examples.ko: 기온이 하루 만에 영하로 곤두박질해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the temperature plunged below zero in just one day.

explain: '곤두박질치다'라고도 많이 말해요. 몸이 거꾸로 떨어질 때뿐 아니라 주가, 성적, 인기가 갑자기 크게 떨어질 때도 써요. 반대로 값이 확 오를 때는 '치솟다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The temperature suddenly plunged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning, and used more often.

phrases.en: I want to revive my plunging popularity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun.

phrases.en: I'm scared my grades will plunge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 생길까 걱정할 때 '-ㄹ까 봐'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ㄹ까 봐', it expresses worry that something bad may happen.

explain_en: People also say '곤두박질치다'. It is used for a body falling head-first, and also when stock prices, grades or popularity suddenly drop a lot. The opposite, when prices shoot up, is '치솟다'.

examples.en: This channel earns its income from advertising fees.

examples.ko: 광고료가 비싸서 작은 가게는 부담이 커요.
examples.en: Ad fees are expensive, so it's a big burden for small shops.
The advertising fee differs depending on the broadcast time slot.

examples.ko: 광고료를 내면 검색 결과 맨 위에 나와요.
examples.en: If you pay an ad fee, you appear at the top of the search results.

examples.ko: 유명한 모델을 쓰면 광고료가 훨씬 올라가요.
examples.en: If you use a famous model, the ad costs go up a lot.
Please tell me the price including the advertising fee.

explain: 신문이나 방송, 사이트가 광고를 실어 주고 받는 돈이라는 느낌이 강해요. 광고를 내는 쪽 입장에서는 '광고비'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Broadcasters receive advertising fees and air the ads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 실어 주는 쪽에서 돈을 받는 입장으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side that carries ads and receives the money.

phrases.en: The shop owner paid an advertising fee to the newspaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 내는 쪽에서 돈을 내는 입장으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side that places the ad and pays.

phrases.en: I spent a lot on advertising this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고를 내는 쪽에서 쓰는 돈을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for money spent by the party running the ad.

explain_en: It carries the sense of money that a newspaper, broadcaster or site charges for running an ad. From the advertiser's side, people also commonly say '광고비'.

examples.ko: 학술지 구독료가 비싸서 학교 도서관을 통해 읽어요.
examples.en: The journal subscription fee is expensive, so I read it through the school library.
The newspaper subscription fee went up again.

examples.ko: 월 구독료를 내면 영화를 무제한으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pay a monthly subscription fee, you can watch unlimited movies.
I set the subscription fee to be paid automatically by card.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 구독료 없이 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this app without a subscription fee.
The subscription fee was a burden, so I cancelled the service.

explain: 신문, 잡지뿐 아니라 요즘은 음악, 영상, 앱 서비스에 내는 정기 요금도 구독료라고 해요. '월 구독료', '구독료를 내다'처럼 써요. 서비스를 그만두는 건 '구독을 해지하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I pay the subscription fee for a video service every month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정기적으로 돈을 낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means paying money on a regular basis.

phrases.en: The monthly subscription fee is 10,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 달마다 내는 요금을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the fee paid each month.

phrases.en: The subscription fee was a burden, so I cancelled my subscription.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서비스 이용을 그만둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you stop using the service.

explain_en: Besides newspapers and magazines, it now also covers regular fees for music, video and app services. You say '월 구독료' and '구독료를 내다'. Quitting a service is '구독을 해지하다'.

examples.en: When prices rise, consumers' purchasing power falls.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 구매력 높은 중산층이 많아요.
examples.en: This country has many middle-class people with high purchasing power.

examples.ko: 월급이 같아도 환율에 따라 구매력은 달라져요.
examples.en: Even with the same salary, purchasing power changes with the exchange rate.

examples.ko: 정부는 청년의 구매력을 높일 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The government is looking for ways to raise young people's purchasing power.

examples.ko: 구매력에 맞는 가격으로 물건을 팔아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to sell goods at prices that match what customers can afford.

examples.ko: 구매력까지 고려하면 이 도시가 더 비싸요.
examples.en: If you take purchasing power into account too, this city is more expensive.

explain: 가진 돈으로 물건을 살 수 있는 힘이에요. 월급이 같아도 물가가 오르면 구매력은 떨어져요. 단순한 소득이나 재산과는 달라요. '구매력이 높다/낮다/떨어지다', '구매력을 높이다'처럼 경제 뉴스에서 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 월급을 올리면 사람들의 구매력을 높일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Raising wages can increase people's purchasing power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 더 많이 살 수 있게 한다는 뜻으로, 경제 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means helping people afford more, used in talk about the economy.

phrases.en: If income is low, purchasing power is low.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살 수 있는 힘이 약하다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the ability to buy things is weak.

phrases.example: 회사는 구매력이 있는 소비자를 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: The company is looking for consumers with purchasing power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 살 돈이 충분한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people who have enough money to buy things.

explain_en: It means how much you can buy with the money you have. Even with the same salary, purchasing power drops when prices rise, so it differs from income or wealth itself. It is common in economic news, as in '구매력이 높다/낮다/떨어지다' and '구매력을 높이다'.

examples.en: The government decided to increase next year's defense spending.
I saw on the news how much the defense spending is.
The debate dragged on because of the defense budget.
The scale of defense spending differs from country to country.
Most of the money spent on defense is tax money.
Voices demanding cuts in defense spending are loud.

explain: 나라를 지키는 일에 쓰는 돈이에요. 뉴스에서 '국방비를 늘리다/줄이다', '국방비 증가'처럼 예산 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '국방 예산'도 있어요.

phrases.en: That country decided to cut its defense spending.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늘리다'의 반대로, 예산 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 늘리다, common in budget news.

phrases.en: The defense budget decreased a little this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국방비'와 비슷한 말이고 예산 계획을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 국방비, often used when talking about budget plans.

phrases.en: I saw news about the increase in defense spending.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사처럼 붙여서 제목이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun phrase, often in headlines and news.

explain_en: It is the money spent on defending the country. In the news it appears in budget talk, such as '국방비를 늘리다/줄이다' and '국방비 증가'. A similar phrase is '국방 예산'.

examples.ko: 정부는 국채를 발행해서 필요한 돈을 마련해요.
examples.en: The government issues government bonds to raise the money it needs.

examples.ko: 국채 금리가 오르면 이자 부담이 커져요.
examples.en: When government bond yields rise, the interest burden grows.

examples.ko: 안전하다고 해서 은퇴 자금을 국채에 넣었어요.
examples.en: Because it's said to be safe, I put my retirement funds into government bonds.

examples.ko: 국채 발행이 늘어서 걱정하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people are worried because government bond issuance has increased.

examples.ko: 국채 만기가 되면 원금과 이자를 받아요.
examples.en: When a government bond matures, you receive principal and interest.

examples.ko: 은행에서 국채에 투자하는 상품을 추천해 줬어요.
examples.en: The bank recommended a product that invests in government bonds.

explain: 나라가 돈을 빌리려고 내는 채권이에요. 나라 빚 전체를 말하는 '국가 채무'와는 구별해서 쓰고, 회사가 내는 '회사채'와 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. '국채를 발행하다', '국채 금리'처럼 경제 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Banks buy a lot of safe government bonds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투자하거나 보유하려고 국채를 산다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means buying government bonds to invest or hold.

phrases.en: The government increased its bond issuance this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경제 뉴스에서 자주 보는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun collocation common in economic news.

phrases.example: 정부는 만기가 되면 국채를 갚아야 해요.
phrases.en: The government must repay the bonds when they mature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌린 돈을 돌려준다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means paying back the borrowed money.

explain_en: This is a bond a country issues to borrow money. Keep it distinct from '국가 채무', which means the nation's debt overall, and it pairs nicely with '회사채' (corporate bond). It shows up in economic news in phrases like '국채를 발행하다' and '국채 금리'.

examples.en: We divided the cake evenly into six pieces.

examples.ko: 모든 학생에게 기회가 균등히 돌아가야 해요.
examples.en: Opportunities should go equally to every student.

examples.ko: 비용을 세 사람이 균등히 부담하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The three of us agreed to share the cost equally.
Please sow the seeds evenly across the field.

examples.ko: 열이 균등히 퍼지도록 팬을 천천히 돌렸어요.
examples.en: I slowly turned the pan so the heat spread evenly.

examples.ko: 이익은 직원들에게 균등히 나눠 줄 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to distribute the profit equally among the employees.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '고르게', '똑같이'를 많이 말하고, '균등히'는 공지나 글에서 볼 수 있는 딱딱한 말이에요. '균등하게'라고도 해요. 반대는 '불균등하게'예요.

phrases.en: We decided to divide the work equally.
phrases.nuance_ko: '균등히'와 뜻은 같고 말할 때 조금 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '균등히' but a bit more natural in speech.

phrases.en: Please sprinkle the salt evenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 흔한 말이고, 분량이나 모양이 한쪽으로 치우치지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday word, for when nothing is lopsided.

phrases.en: Please share the candy equally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양이나 수가 같다는 점을 쉽고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple, soft way to say the amounts are the same.

explain_en: In daily talk people say '고르게' or '똑같이'; 균등히 is a stiffer word you see in notices and writing. You can also say '균등하게'. The opposite is '불균등하게'.

en: to be slight; to be very small (amount, margin, difference)

examples.en: The score difference between the two teams is slim.
I missed first place by a narrow margin.
Our candidate is leading by a slim margin.

examples.ko: 두 제품은 가격 차이가 근소해서 고르기 어려워요.
examples.en: The price difference between the two products is tiny, so it's hard to choose.

examples.ko: 표 차이는 근소했지만 결과는 바뀌지 않았어요.
examples.en: The vote gap was slim, but the result didn't change.
I thought it would be close, but the gap was big.

explain: 점수, 표, 가격처럼 수나 양의 차이가 아주 작을 때 써요. '근소한 차이로 이기다/지다', '근소하게 앞서다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 사람이나 기분에는 쓰지 않고, 반대로 차이가 클 때는 '크다'나 '현저하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Our team won by a narrow margin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수 차이가 아주 작게 이긴 경기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a game won by a very small score gap.
phrases.en_equiv: to win by a narrow margin

phrases.example: 어제 조사에서는 그 후보가 근소하게 앞섰어요.
phrases.en: In yesterday's poll, that candidate led by a small margin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금만 앞서 있을 때 부사형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, used when someone is ahead by only a little.

phrases.en: The gap in support between the two candidates is slight.
phrases.nuance_ko: '차이가 근소하다'로 수나 양의 차이가 아주 작다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that a difference in number or amount is very small.

explain_en: It is used when a difference in numbers or amounts, such as scores, votes or prices, is very small. '근소한 차이로 이기다/지다' and '근소하게 앞서다' are common pairings. It is not used for people or feelings, and for a big difference people say '크다' or '현저하다'.

p.n: 적다 just says the difference is small; 근소하다 stresses it is razor-thin.

examples.ko: 요즘 금값이 너무 올라서 반지 사기 부담돼요.
examples.en: Gold prices have risen so much that buying a ring is a burden.
The price of gold changes a little every day.

examples.ko: 금값도 한 번 오르면 쉽게 안 내려요.
examples.en: Once the price of gold goes up, it doesn't come down easily.
The news said gold prices hit a record high.

examples.ko: 금값 때문에 결혼반지 가격도 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Because of the price of gold, wedding ring prices went up a lot too.
I checked the gold price yesterday and it had gone up again.

explain: '금값이 오르다, 내리다, 떨어지다'처럼 가격이 움직이는 동사와 같이 써요. 금 가격 이야기라서 뉴스와 금은방 이야기에 자주 나와요. 발음은 사이시옷 때문에 [금깝]이에요.

phrases.en: Apples are crazy expensive these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 귀해지거나 값이 많이 올랐을 때 과장해서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggerated way to say something has become scarce or has shot up in price.

explain_en: It goes with verbs of price movement like '금값이 오르다, 내리다, 떨어지다'. Since it is about the price of gold, it shows up often in the news and at jewelry shops. Because of the sai-siot, it is pronounced [금깝].

examples.ko: 금융권은 올해 신입 사원을 많이 뽑는대요.
examples.en: I hear the financial sector is hiring many new employees this year.

examples.ko: 정부가 금융권 대출 규정을 바꾸기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to change the loan rules for the financial sector.
After I graduate, I want to work in the financial industry.

examples.ko: 금융권 전체가 금리 인상 때문에 긴장하고 있어요.
examples.en: The whole financial sector is on edge because of the interest rate hike.

examples.ko: 은행과 보험사 같은 금융권 회사는 연봉이 높은 편이에요.
examples.en: Financial companies such as banks and insurers tend to pay high salaries.
I heard that the interest rate is higher at second-tier financial institutions than at banks.

explain: 은행, 보험, 증권 같은 금융 회사들을 한데 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '제1금융권'은 은행, '제2금융권'은 보험사나 저축은행 같은 곳을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The first-tier financial sector usually means banks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은행을 가리키는 말이고, 보험사나 저축은행은 '제2금융권'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This means banks, while insurers and savings banks are called 제2금융권.

phrases.en: The interest on financial-sector loans has gone up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은행 같은 금융 회사에서 받는 대출을 묶어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to loans from banks and similar companies as a group.

phrases.en: My friend got a job in the financial sector after graduating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은행, 보험, 증권 같은 곳에 일자리를 구했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means getting a job at a bank, insurer, or securities firm.
phrases.en_equiv: to get a job in finance

explain_en: It is a collective term for financial companies such as banks, insurers and securities firms. '제1금융권' refers to banks, and '제2금융권' to places like insurance companies and savings banks.

examples.en: The number of tourists dropped sharply this year.
When it rains, the shop's customers drop sharply.

examples.ko: 출생아 수가 급감하는 것이 큰 문제예요.
examples.en: The sharp drop in the number of births is a big problem.
I heard the factory closed because demand plummeted.
Nobody knew the popularity would plummet.
It is a month when prices rose but sales dropped sharply.

explain: '줄다'보다 훨씬 갑작스럽고 크게 줄 때 써요. 뉴스에서 매출, 인구, 관광객 같은 숫자가 확 줄었을 때 자주 나와요. 반대는 '급증하다'예요.

phrases.en: The number of children is dropping sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 크게 줄어드는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is in the middle of dropping sharply.

phrases.en: The population dropped a lot this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '급감하다'보다 이 말이 더 쉽고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, this is easier and more natural than '급감하다'.

phrases.en: Customers dropped sharply, so the shop closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-어서'를 붙여 줄어든 일을 이유로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-어서' links the sharp drop to a result or reason.

explain_en: It is used when something falls much more suddenly and by a larger amount than 줄다. It often appears in news when numbers like sales, population, or tourists drop sharply. The opposite is 급증하다.

examples.ko: 요즘 채소 값이 급등해서 장보기가 무서워요.
examples.en: Vegetable prices have soared lately, so grocery shopping scares me.
The exchange rate soared in a single day.

examples.ko: 집값이 급등하면 젊은 사람들이 집을 사기 어려워요.
examples.en: When housing prices soar, it's hard for young people to buy a home.
Because oil prices soared, prices in general went up too.
The news explained why the stock price soared.

examples.ko: 기름값이 급등하지 않도록 정부가 대책을 내놨어요.
examples.en: The government came up with measures to keep fuel prices from soaring.

explain: 가격, 환율, 주가처럼 숫자로 나타나는 것이 갑자기 크게 오를 때 써요. 반대말은 '급락하다'예요. 사람의 키나 나이에는 쓰지 않고, 일상에서는 '확 오르다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Heating costs shot up when winter came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 갑자기 크게 오른 것을 말할 때 쓰는 편한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday way to say something rose sharply.

phrases.en: House prices have skyrocketed, so I can't move.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급등하다'보다 훨씬 더 심하게 오를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stronger than '급등하다', for extremely steep rises.

phrases.en: Gas prices have been surging lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 오르는 흐름을 말하며 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a surging trend, common in news reports.

explain_en: It is used when something measured in numbers, such as prices, exchange rates or stock prices, suddenly rises a lot. The opposite is '급락하다'. It is not used for a person's height or age, and in daily speech people also say '확 오르다'.

examples.en: When it gets hot, ice cream sales soar.

examples.ko: 어제 올린 영상이 인기 순위에서 급상승하고 있어요.
examples.en: The video I posted yesterday is rising fast in the popularity rankings.
When a search term shoots up the rankings, people get curious.

examples.ko: 이 회사 주가가 한 달 만에 급상승했어요.
examples.en: This company's stock price soared in just a month.
The exchange rate soared, so I changed my travel plans.

examples.ko: 급상승한 물가 때문에 장 보기가 부담돼요.
examples.en: Because prices have soared, grocery shopping is a burden.

explain: 반대말은 '급락하다'예요. 물가, 주가, 순위, 온도처럼 숫자나 순위가 갑자기 오를 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '확 오르다', '뛰다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Thanks to the drama, the actor's popularity soared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기나 관심이 갑자기 커질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for popularity or interest suddenly growing.

phrases.en: I checked the rapidly rising search terms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 많이 검색된 말을 가리켜요. 인터넷에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to search terms that suddenly got many searches; common online.

phrases.en: The temperature shot up in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '급상승하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say 급상승하다.

explain_en: Its opposite is '급락하다' (plunge). It is used when numbers or rankings, like prices, stocks, ranks or temperatures, rise suddenly. In casual talk people also say '확 오르다' or '뛰다'.

examples.en: I am curious about the secret of this company's rapid growth.

examples.ko: 온라인 쇼핑 시장이 급성장을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: The online shopping market continues its rapid growth.
Difficulties always follow rapid growth.

examples.ko: 한류 덕분에 한국어 학원들이 급성장의 시기를 맞았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the Korean wave, Korean language schools entered a period of rapid growth.
Traffic became congested because of the city's rapid growth.

examples.ko: 급성장한 기업 중에서 살아남은 곳은 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Not many of the rapidly grown companies have survived.

explain: '급성장'은 기업, 시장, 산업의 이야기에서 뉴스 용어로 자주 나와요. 사람이 크는 것은 '쑥쑥 자라다'가 더 자연스러워요. '급성장을 이루다', '급성장을 겪다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: This company achieved rapid growth in three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 커졌다는 결과를 말할 때 '이루다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '이루다' when stating the result that something grew fast.

phrases.example: 급성장 덕분에 직원이 두 배로 늘었어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to the rapid growth, the number of employees doubled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠른 성장이 좋은 결과를 가져왔을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when rapid growth led to a good result.

phrases.en: After the rapid growth, the office became too small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 커진 다음에 생긴 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to talk about what happened after fast growth.

explain_en: 급성장 is a common news term for companies, markets and industries. For people growing up, 쑥쑥 자라다 sounds more natural. It goes in phrases like 급성장을 이루다 and 급성장을 겪다.

examples.en: This month's pay is lower than I expected.
How much is left after subtracting tax from the pay?
The company sends the pay on the 25th of every month.
The insurance premium varies depending on the salary amount.
A new employee's pay differs from company to company.

examples.ko: 급여액과 실제로 받는 돈은 조금 달라요.
examples.en: The stated pay and the money you actually receive are a bit different.

explain: 월급이라는 말보다 서류나 회사에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 친구끼리는 '월급'이라고 하고, 급여 명세서나 계약서에서는 '급여액'을 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: Be sure to check the wage amount before signing the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 계약서에서 받을 돈을 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking the amount to be paid on documents or contracts.

phrases.en: My pay went up a little this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 돈이 늘었을 때 써요. 반대는 '줄다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the pay increases; the opposite is 줄다.

phrases.en: My salary came in, so I bought my friend a meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 쉬운 말로, 일상 대화에서는 '급여액'보다 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word with the same meaning, used far more than 급여액 in daily talk.

explain_en: It is a more formal word than '월급', used in documents and by companies. Friends say '월급', while '급여액' is common on pay stubs and contracts.

examples.en: A commemorative coin came out to mark the Olympics.
I received a commemorative coin as a gift from my grandfather.

examples.ko: 기념주화는 일반 동전과 달리 모양이 특별해요.
examples.en: Unlike ordinary coins, commemorative coins have special designs.
I stood in line at the bank to buy a commemorative coin.
The tournament logo is engraved on the commemorative coin.
My friend collects commemorative coins as a hobby.

explain: 행사나 사건을 기념하려고 특별하게 만든 동전이에요. 뉴스에서는 '기념주화를 발행하다'라고 하고, 일상에서는 쉽게 '기념 동전'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 여행 가서 기념 동전을 하나 샀어요.
phrases.en: I bought a commemorative coin on my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기념주화'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, everyday way to say 기념주화.

phrases.en: The bank issued a new commemorative coin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 만드는 쪽을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase from the issuer's side.

phrases.en: Collecting commemorative coins is my hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about hobbies.

explain_en: It is a coin specially made to mark an event or occasion. In the news you will hear '기념주화를 발행하다' (to issue a commemorative coin), and in daily talk people also say '기념 동전'.

examples.en: I went to the bank to claim my lottery winnings.
The prize was so big that I couldn't believe it.

examples.ko: 친구가 당첨금으로 부모님께 집을 사 드렸어요.
examples.en: My friend bought his parents a house with his winnings.
I found out that tax is charged on winnings.
Be sure to check the payout date for the winnings.
I received a hundred thousand won in prize money at the event.

explain: '상금'은 대회에서 이겨서 받는 돈이고, '당첨금'은 복권이나 추첨에 뽑혀서 받는 돈이에요. 받는 방법이 달라서 말이 달라요. 복권은 '1등 당첨금'처럼 등수와 함께 말해요.

phrases.en: The first-prize money is a really large amount.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복권은 등수와 함께 당첨금을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For lotteries, the prize money is named with its rank.

phrases.example: 그는 복권 당첨금을 받고 집을 샀어요.
phrases.en: He received the lottery prize and bought a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당첨된 돈을 손에 얻는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means actually getting the prize money.

phrases.en: You need an ID to claim the prize money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 은행 등에서 당첨된 돈을 직접 받으러 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you go in person to collect the prize, for example at a bank.

explain_en: 상금 is money you receive for winning a contest, while 당첨금 is money you receive by being drawn in a lottery or raffle. The words differ because the way of winning differs. Lotteries use forms like 1등 당첨금, with the rank.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 대주주가 경영에 직접 참여하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company's major shareholder decided to take part in management directly.

examples.ko: 대주주들이 주식을 팔면 주가가 크게 떨어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the major shareholders sell their shares, the stock price can fall a lot.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 작은 회사의 대주주라서 회의에 꼭 참석해요.
examples.en: My uncle is a major shareholder of a small company, so he always attends the meetings.

examples.ko: 새로운 대주주는 회사 이름을 바꾸겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The new major shareholder said he would change the company's name.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 대주주의 책임에 대한 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was a story about the responsibility of major shareholders on the news.
When the company got into trouble, they asked the major shareholder for help.

explain: 회사의 주식을 많이 가진 사람이나 회사를 말해요. 주식을 조금 가진 사람은 '소액주주'라고 해요. 경제 뉴스에서 '최대주주'와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: That person is the largest shareholder of the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 많은 주식을 가진 사람을 말하고 경제 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the person holding the most shares and often appears in economic news.

phrases.en: The major shareholders hold more than half of the shares.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대주주가 가진 주식의 비율을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the proportion of shares held by a major shareholder.

phrases.en: He became a major shareholder of this company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주식을 많이 사서 큰 몫을 갖게 됐을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has bought many shares and holds a large part.

explain_en: It refers to a person or company that holds a large share of a company's stock. Someone with only a small number of shares is called a '소액주주'. It often appears in economic news alongside '최대주주'.

examples.en: My father runs a wholesale fruit business.

examples.ko: 도매업은 한 번에 많이 사고팔아서 값이 싸요.
examples.en: Wholesale deals in large amounts at a time, so prices are low.
My uncle worked in wholesale and then opened his own shop.
There are many wholesale merchants in this market.

examples.ko: 도매업이 어려워져서 문을 닫는 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Wholesale has gotten harder, so some places are closing.
Do you know the difference between wholesale and retail?

explain: 반대말은 소비자에게 직접 파는 '소매업'이에요. 그 일을 하는 가게나 사람은 '도매상'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: My uncle is in the vegetable wholesale business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 직업으로 한다고 말할 때 '하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 하다 to say what business someone runs.

phrases.example: 가게 주인이 도매상에서 물건을 사 와요.
phrases.en: The shop owner buys goods from a wholesaler.
phrases.nuance_ko: 업종보다 그 일을 하는 가게나 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the shop or person doing the business rather than the business type.

phrases.example: 소매업은 손님에게 직접 물건을 파는 일이에요.
phrases.en: Retail is selling goods directly to customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말로, 소비자에게 직접 파는 장사를 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite word, meaning selling directly to consumers.

explain_en: The opposite is '소매업' (retail), which sells directly to consumers. A shop or person doing that work is also called a '도매상' (wholesaler).

examples.ko: 머리를 직접 잘랐더니 길이가 들쑥날쑥 달라요.
examples.en: I cut my hair myself, and the lengths came out uneven.

examples.ko: 요즘 퇴근 시간이 들쑥날쑥이라 약속을 못 잡아요.
examples.en: The time I leave work is all over the place lately, so I can't make plans.

examples.ko: 글씨가 들쑥날쑥 써져서 보기 안 좋아요.
examples.en: The writing came out uneven and looks bad.
My test scores keep coming out up and down, and I'm worried.
The hedge has grown unevenly.

examples.ko: 제 한 달 수입은 늘 들쑥날쑥이에요.
examples.en: My monthly income is always irregular.

explain: 길이, 크기, 시간, 점수처럼 고르지 않고 들쭉날쭉한 모습을 말해요. 부사지만 '들쑥날쑥이에요'처럼 '이다'를 붙여 쓰기도 해요. '들쭉날쭉'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The heights of my classmates are uneven.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들쑥날쑥'과 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Interchangeable with '들쑥날쑥'.

phrases.en: My hair got cut unevenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 동사를 꾸미는 말이 돼서 어떻게 했는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게' it modifies a verb to say how something was done.

phrases.en: The ground on this road is not even.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 평범하게 말하는 표현이라 어떤 상황에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, plainer phrase usable in any situation.

explain_en: It describes things that are uneven or inconsistent, such as length, size, time or scores. Although it is an adverb, it can take '이다', as in '들쑥날쑥이에요'. '들쭉날쭉' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.en: Sales are poor today because it's raining.
The shop's sales went up a lot compared to last month.
Boss, how much did we make in sales today?

examples.ko: 새 메뉴를 내놓은 뒤로 매상이 두 배가 됐어요.
examples.en: Since we launched the new menu, sales have doubled.

examples.ko: 매상을 올리려고 할인 행사를 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold a discount event to boost sales.

examples.ko: 직원이 매상을 잘못 적어서 계산이 안 맞아요.
examples.en: An employee recorded the sales wrong, so the numbers don't add up.

explain: 가게에서 하루나 한 달 동안 물건을 팔아 번 돈을 말해요. 식당이나 작은 가게에서 입말로 많이 쓰고, 회사나 뉴스에서는 '매출'이 더 흔해요. '매상이 오르다, 매상이 떨어지다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: We raised our sales with a new menu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 주인이 노력해서 팔린 돈을 늘릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a shop owner works to increase takings.

phrases.en: Ice cream sales drop in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매상이 오르다'의 반대로 장사가 잘 안될 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 매상이 오르다, for when business is slow.

phrases.en: Our company's sales grew this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 같지만 '매출'은 회사나 뉴스에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but more common for companies and news.

explain_en: It means the money a shop takes in from sales over a day or month. It is common in spoken Korean at restaurants and small shops, while companies and the news prefer '매출'. It is often used as '매상이 오르다' or '매상이 떨어지다'.
